qualitative_system_behaviour.item: As nacelle angle changes from 90 deg helicopter mode to 0 deg airplane mode, control inputs are mixed between rotor cyclic/collective pitch and aerodynamic surfaces through mechanical linkages.
Hover roll is described as using differential rotor collective pitch.
Hover yaw is described as using differential longitudinal cyclic pitch, tilting the proprotor axes in opposite directions.
The wing interconnect driveshaft synchronizes rotor speed and can allow either engine to drive both rotors after a single-engine failure.
The lowest blade in-plane natural frequency is described as above the one-per-revolution operating speed.
